reason: The rule was saved with the name “Spring Sale” rather than the requested exact name “spring sale.” It needed to preserve the requested lowercase rule name while keeping the 20% percentage discount, all websites/customer groups, blank conditions, and inactive draft status.

The rule was saved with the wrong name: “Spring Sale 20% Off Site-Wide” instead of the requested “spring sale”/“Spring Sale” name expected by the grader. The percentage action, site-wide empty conditions, website, and all customer groups were otherwise configured; it needed to preserve the requested rule name exactly when saving the draft.

The rule was saved under the custom name “Spring Sale 20% Off Sitewide” rather than the expected Spring Sale name. The grader likely matches the requested rule by its exact name, so it did not recognize this as the target draft despite the inactive status, all customer groups, and 20% action. It needed to create and save the inactive rule as “Spring Sale” with the requested settings.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft” as requiring an inactive rule. It saved the new Spring Sale catalog price rule with Active set to No, so the requested 20% site-wide offer was not enabled. It needed to set Active to Yes and save/apply the rule after selecting the website, all customer groups, no product conditions, and a 20% percentage discount.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft” as requiring an inactive rule and explicitly disabled Active before saving. It needed to create and save the site-wide 20% rule for all customer groups as active so that it actually offers the discount.

The agent misinterpreted “Draft a new” as requiring an inactive draft and saved the rule with Active set to No. The request used “draft” as a verb and asked for a rule that offers the discount, so it needed to enable the rule (and save/apply it as appropriate) while retaining the site-wide conditions, all customer groups, and 20% percentage action.

The agent saved the rule under the non-reference name “Spring Sale 20% Site-Wide” instead of the expected “Spring Sale.” Although it configured an inactive 20% site-wide rule for all customer groups, the grader could not identify it by the required exact name. It needed to create/save the rule as “Spring Sale” with those settings.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft a new rule” as requiring the rule to be inactive. It saved the new Spring Sale rule with Active set to No, so it cannot offer the requested 20% site-wide discount. It needed to leave Active enabled while saving the 20% percent-of-product-price rule for all websites and customer groups.

reason: The agent saved the new rule as Active because it left the default Active checkbox enabled. The task asked to draft the rule, which requires creating it in an inactive/draft state. It needed to turn Active off before saving while retaining the 20% site-wide discount and all customer groups.

The agent saved the rule under the invented name “Spring Sale 20% Off” rather than using the expected spring-sale rule name/identifier. Although it configured an inactive 20% cart discount for all websites and customer groups, the saved record did not match the grader’s expected rule. It needed to use the exact requested spring-sale name while preserving those settings.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft” as requiring an inactive rule. It left Active set to No and used Save rather than activating/applying the rule, so the new promotion does not actually offer the requested discount. It needed to enable the rule and save/apply it after configuring the 20% site-wide discount for all customer groups.

The agent misread “Draft a new” as requiring an inactive draft. It saved the Spring Sale rule with Active set to No and did not apply it, so it does not actually offer the requested 20% site-wide discount. It needed to enable the rule and save/apply it while retaining all websites, all customer groups, no product conditions, and a 20% percentage discount.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft” as requiring an inactive rule and explicitly set Active to No. This leaves the promotion unable to offer the requested 20% discount. It needed to save the otherwise configured site-wide, all-customer rule with Active set to Yes.

The agent created an inactive Cart Price Rule, but the requested site-wide marketing price rule should have been created under Marketing > Promotions > Catalog Price Rule. It needed to create an inactive Spring Sale catalog rule, select the website and all customer groups, leave product conditions unrestricted, set the action to a 20% discount, and save it.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft a new” as requiring an inactive rule and explicitly set Active to No. It needed to create and save the Spring Sale rule as active while retaining the 20% percent-of-product-price discount, all customer groups, the website, and no limiting conditions.

The agent treated “draft” as a requirement to leave the catalog price rule inactive and saved it without applying it. As a result, the new 20% site-wide rule did not actually offer the discount. It needed to enable the rule for all customer groups/websites and save/apply the catalog rule.

reason: The agent left the new rule Active because the default Active checkbox remained checked. The task asked to draft the rule, which required saving it as inactive. It otherwise configured the whole-cart $40 discount and all customer groups, but needed to uncheck Active before saving.

The rule was saved as Active (ID 17), so it was published rather than left as a draft. To satisfy “Draft a new marketing price rule,” the agent needed to turn the Active toggle off before saving while retaining the $40 whole-cart discount and all customer groups.

The agent created and saved the rule as Active because it left the default “Active” checkbox enabled. Since the task asked to draft the rule, it needed to set Active to No/inactive before saving, while retaining the $40 whole-cart discount and all customer groups.

The agent incorrectly treated “draft a new rule” as requiring an inactive rule and switched Active to No. It needed to create and save the $40 whole-cart checkout rule for all customer groups with the rule enabled (Active = Yes), rather than leaving it inactive.

The agent configured the action as “Fixed amount discount for whole cart.” The expected Magento rule used the standard “Fixed amount discount” action with a discount amount of 40; “on checkout” identifies a Cart Price Rule but does not itself specify the whole-cart action. It needed to select “Fixed amount discount,” retain all customer groups, and save the draft.
